name: Affix Loot Generator
description: The dice behind the drop. inventory.loot_table decides WHAT falls out of a monster; this component decides HOW GOOD the copy is — rarity tier first, then affix count from rarity, then each affix rolled inside its tier's value range. Splitting this from loot_table matters because drop tables are content (designers edit them per monster, per zone) while affix math is system (tuned globally, once, and feared thereafter). It does not own where the item goes: the finished item is emitted, and inventory.core_inventory or inventory.slotted_bag decides whether it fits. It also refuses to render — rarity color and the stat card belong to ui.hud and the tooltip layer, and a generator that picks colors has opinions no loot system should have.

inputs.name: rarityWeights
inputs.description: Relative weights per rarity tier. Weights, not percentages, so adding a tier never requires renormalizing the others.

inputs.name: affixCountByTier
inputs.description: How many affixes each tier rolls. The jump from 0 to 2 is the moment loot starts feeling like loot; keep it early.

inputs.name: luckStatInfluence
inputs.description: How strongly a player luck stat shifts rarity weights toward the top. Zero by default because luck stats compound: a small shift every kill is a large shift every hour.

inputs.name: affixPoolTags
inputs.description: Restricts which affix families may roll (e.g. ['fire', 'defense']). Empty means the full pool; zone- or monster-themed pools keep drops legible.

outputs.name: lastGeneratedItem
outputs.description: The full rolled item: base id, tier, affix list with rolled values.
